Looking at the recent Morning Consult tracker data, I see values stabilizing around 42.5-42.9% in the last three releases (early-to-mid August). The series has been notably stable in the low 42s after declining from mid-July highs around 45%.

The search results reveal important context: the Tampa Free Press article (Aug 10) confirms Morning Consult's latest was at ~43% approve / 55% disapprove, matching "record lows recorded earlier this summer." This suggests the decline to the 42-43 range predated the Iran war news that broke around Aug 16-17.

Other pollsters show sharper drops: Al Jazeera/Reuters reports 33%, Civiqs shows 35%, and YouGov shows 33%. However, these are largely adult-based polls or have different house effects. Morning Consult's registered voter base has consistently read higher than these other polls (the question itself notes the RV base differs by "several points" from the adult base). The 7-10 point gap between Morning Consult RV and Civiqs RV suggests substantial house-effect differences.

The Iran war development is a significant negative shock, but Morning Consult's RV panel has shown remarkable stability — the last three values are within 0.4 points of each other. No search result specifically mentions a Morning Consult decline in late August, which could indicate either modest further movement or that it hasn't been newsworthy enough given the more dramatic drops in other polls.

I expect a modest further decline from the ~42.7% recent average, reflecting partial absorption of the Iran war impact, but less dramatic than other pollsters given Morning Consult's stable RV methodology and existing low base. The standard deviation accounts for weekly volatility (~1.0), the ~2.5 week forecast horizon, and additional uncertainty from the evolving geopolitical situation.

{"mean": 41.5, "sd": 1.5}
